findings.description: Unbounded memory allocation in BER length decoding without size validation
findings.reasoning: The BER decoder reads a variable-length encoding of the content length without validating the resulting value. When firstOctet > 128, it reads up to 127 bytes that represent the length. These bytes are assembled into an integer using bit shifting with no upper bound check. This length value is then passed to readFromStream() which will attempt to allocate that many bytes in memory. An attacker can craft a malicious BER message with a length field encoding an extremely large value (up to 2^(127*8) bytes), causing unbounded memory allocation and denial of service. The comment on line 1671 even acknowledges "missing check on maximum size".
